immediate_conceptual_response: Keep doors shut, check temperatures, move food to working cold space, stop using at-risk items, tell the lead.
resilience_requirement: Written hold-or-discard decisions set by a professional; monitoring and service contacts.
dependency: Maintenance service, cold storage, food-safety professional

immediate_conceptual_response: Switch to a manual order and payment routine; keep a paper list; reconcile once it recovers.
resilience_requirement: Offline plan, backup pad and paper, trained staff.

immediate_conceptual_response: Pause water-dependent work; use bottled water for essentials; decide whether food service can safely continue.
resilience_requirement: Written closure triggers and handwashing and sanitation rules set by authorities.

immediate_conceptual_response: Protect cold items, stop fryers safely, use backup light, decide whether to continue or close.
resilience_requirement: Safe shutdown steps, backup lighting, cold-hold discipline.

immediate_conceptual_response: Use alternates, simplify the menu, or sell out of affected items honestly.
resilience_requirement: Second supplier option, ordering buffer, clear substitution rules that respect D-54.

immediate_conceptual_response: Offer bottles or cans if available, non-alcoholic choices, or other draft lines; tell guests plainly.
resilience_requirement: Backup serving plan, maintenance contacts, trained staff.

immediate_conceptual_response: Remove it from the menu, offer a simple alternate, and keep pairings honest.
resilience_requirement: Defined fallback dishes and menu update routine; no unapproved substitutions.

immediate_conceptual_response: Reassign tasks, simplify service, call in cross-trained staff, or reduce the menu.
resilience_requirement: Cross-training and written station guides; no invented staffing counts.
dependency: Staffing plan, labor attorney for questions
